prompt: Final challenge! 🏆 The Pong works from start to finish... but to play it you need someone on the other side.
You're going to program a rival: the right paddle will move on its own, following the ball. That way you can play against the machine!
The idea: if the ball is higher than the middle of the paddle (`palaDretaY + 40`, pala dreta = right paddle), the paddle moves up a bit. If it's lower, it moves down a bit.

Write the two `if`s on the yellow line. Move the paddle 4 pixels each time: any faster and there'd be no way to beat it! (Tip for winning: if the ball hits the edge of your paddle, it comes off at a sharper angle.)
hints: The middle of the paddle is `palaDretaY + 40`. Compare `pilotaY` with it.
One `if` with `pilotaY < palaDretaY + 40` that subtracts 4 from `palaDretaY`, and another with `>` that adds 4.
`if (pilotaY < palaDretaY + 40) { palaDretaY = palaDretaY - 4; }` and `if (pilotaY > palaDretaY + 40) { palaDretaY = palaDretaY + 4; }`
rival.success: You've got a real rival! Click the game and play with W and S. Can you beat it?

prompt: YOU DID IT! The Pong machine works again. 🎉
You've learned coordinates, variables, the game loop, `if`, comparisons, bounces, `&&`, counters... and you programmed a rival. That's real programming!
All the code you see is real C, the same that people who make video games with raylib use. And the match goes on: click the game and play against your rival with W and S!
Press «⬇ Download your main.c» and take your Pong with you: it's yours!
Thanks for fixing my arcade. Come back to the arcade whenever you like: other machines will light up soon!

checks.moves: The right paddle doesn't move. Write two `if`s that make it go up and down depending on where the ball is.
checks.fair: The paddle can't teleport! Instead of `palaDretaY = pilotaY`, add or subtract 4 every frame.
checks.neverMisses: The right paddle still lets the ball past. Check that it goes up when the ball is higher (`<`) and down when it's lower (`>`).
